stages.title: Profit maximisation
stages.sub: Draw the cost and revenue curves and read off the output where profit is greatest.

steps.q: You know the marginal cost of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd... unit made. If you plot each of these against output, what do you get?
steps.right: A curve showing cost per extra unit
steps.wrong: A curve showing total cost so far
steps.hint: Each point is the cost of just one more unit, not everything made so far.

steps.q: You already know AVC and ATC fall then rise, and that MC cuts them at their lowest points. If you plot AVC and ATC at every output level, what do you get?
steps.right: Two U-shaped curves, both crossed by MC at their minimum
steps.wrong: Two straight lines that never meet MC
steps.hint: Use the shape and the crossing point you already know about.

steps.q: You know AR is the price line and comes from the same data as TR and MR. If you plot the price the firm charges at every output level, what do you get?
steps.right: A curve showing the price, which is also the demand curve
steps.wrong: A curve showing total revenue at every output
steps.hint: Price per unit sold is what AR actually measures.

steps.hint: Recall how MR sits relative to AR once output rises above zero.
